html:
The Ngaliwurru are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, in the rugged sandstone country around the Victoria River near Timber Creek.

Their close neighbours are the Jaminjung, whose language is very close to theirs, and the Ngarinman and Gurindji further upriver. From the 1880s huge cattle stations took over the Victoria River district, and Aboriginal people became the unpaid or poorly paid stock workers on which those stations ran.

The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Their wider history is told in Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Ngaliwurru are an Aboriginal people of the Northern Territory, in the rugged sandstone country around the Victoria River near Timber Creek.
